title: Live updates: Potential 2028 Democratic contenders discuss future after the party’s midterm victories
text:
Live updates: Potential 2028 Democratic contenders discuss future after the party’s midterm victories 
 BREAKING: FAA orders nationwide ground stop ‘due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety’ 
 LIVE COVERAGE Updated 2 hours ago Live updates: Potential 2028 Democratic contenders discuss future after the party’s midterm victories
 Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., says he will challenge Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., for Senate majority leader.
 Chris Van Hollen challenges Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader 01:46 
 Save Add NBC News to Google Updated November 13, 2026, 3:39 PM EST By NBC News What to know today 
 MAJORITY DEMOCRATS: Potential 2028 contenders are speaking today at a conference in Colorado hosted by the group Majority Democrats, including Sens. Chris Van Hollen, Raphael Warnock, Ruben Gallego and Cory Booker, former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg and Rep. Ro Khanna.
 SCHUMER CHALLENGER: Van Hollen, D-Md., announced he will run for Senate majority leader , becoming the first to challenge Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., for the position.
 ASYLUM CLAIMS: The Supreme Court agreed to decide whether President Donald Trump has the authority to ban asylum claims at the southern border.
 NVIDIA FALLOUT: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick agreed yesterday to testify before Congress over national security concerns regarding the expanding Nvidia scandal. Republican committee chairs told former CEO Jensen Huang and a lawyer for the company that they must agree by this evening to give closed-door testimony or face subpoenas. 
 NEW UPDATES 2h ago / 3:39 PM EST Van Hollen says he won't run for president in 2028 
 Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., told reporters this afternoon that he was "no longer pursuing" a 2028 presidential campaign and instead will focus on his effort to become Senate Democrats' next majority leader. 
 “I believe that the size and scale of these majorities provides an opportunity for the United States Senate to answer the call with the American people,” Van Hollen said, later definitively adding, "I'm not running in 2028." 
 Van Hollen, who officially announced his bid for majority leader yesterday, had previously told NBC News that he was still "kicking the tires" on a potential 2028 run. 
 He said today that he spoke to Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., and that the pair understand "this will be a competition" as Schumer tries to earn another stint of leading the caucus. 
 Show more "I think it's important to give Senate Democrats a choice," Van Hollen said. "That's what we just gave voters all over the country, a choice. They chose change, and I think that the Democratic Caucus needs to be open to new ideas." 
 Van Hollen called himself the "underdog in this race," adding that the "majority leader has lots of powers of incumbency to try to, you know, make deals or agreements with people." 
 "That's actually part of the problem with the process," he said. "But I can tell you that a lot of my colleagues want to see a whole different approach to governing in the United States Senate and in the Senate Democratic Caucus." 
 Van Hollen, who said in an interview with MS NOW last night that "over 10" senators have privately backed him for the role, told reporters today that "I'm not going to put out a number," but that he had just heard from more senators who will support his bid. 
 He specifically noted the endorsement of Sen.-elect Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota, who wrote in a post on X today that Van Hollen is "the leader and fighter we need to bring about real change, so no American is left behind." Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan, another newcomer to the Senate, also pledged his support to Van Hollen last night. 
 "As you well know, the majority of the new members, fresh off the campaign trail, fresh off listening to their constituents, have said they will not support the current majority leader for re-election, and they are answering the call of the American people for change," Van Hollen said. 
 2h ago / 3:35 PM EST Democratic Rep.-elect Brian Poindexter faces investigation over sexual harassment allegation 
 The House Democratic campaign arm has initiated an investigation into Democratic Rep.-elect Brian Poindexter following accusations that he made an inappropriate comment to a campaign staffer ahead of his victory in Ohio’s 7th District.
 Julie Merz, the executive director of the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, confirmed the investigation in a statement Friday afternoon.
 Rep.-elect Brian Poindexter at the Capitol on Monday.   Andrew Harnik / Getty 
 Read the full story here. 
 2h ago / 3:06 PM EST Incoming Judiciary Chairman Jamie Raskin details focus on 'MAGA corruption and authoritarianism' 
 Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md., who is expected to become chairman of the House Judiciary Committee in January, said in a letter to his colleagues on Friday that the new Congress will put a focus on “MAGA corruption and authoritarianism” and his committee will “exploring all the tools of the Majority” once Democrats take over the reins.
 After recounting some of Democrats work when they were in the minority, Raskin writes that “all of these successes are small potatoes compared to what we will need to do to restore the rule of law and legislate against the disgraceful corruption of the government once we actually have the gavels.”
 The House Judiciary Committee, he writes, will be “employing all of the tools of the Majority to extirpate bribery, kickbacks, inside dealing and sweetheart contracts in government; rein in ICE and its savage, lawless attacks on American communities; rebuild the Department of Justice and the FBI on principles of public integrity, respect for the professional standards of the Bar and respect for the rights of federal workers; bring long-overdue ethics reform and a $50 gift ban to the Supreme Court; and protect our most precious birthright possessions: the Constitution, the rule of law under it, our political democracy and all the freedoms protected by the Bill of Rights.”
 Show more The letter asks his colleagues for their support of his nomination, but the ask is somewhat of a formality as Raskin isn’t expected to face a challenge for the position. 
 “I respectfully and humbly ask for your support for me to carry on this crucial work by electing me to be the Chair of the Judiciary Committee. I will continue to work in a collaborative way with the remarkable Members of our Committee through brainstorming, planning and strategizing, always working to use and expand the talents of our Members, especially the new ones raring to get going,” Raskin writes.
 Politico first reported on the letter . 
 2h ago / 3:00 PM EST Rep. Lauren Boebert, conservative firebrand from Colorado, loses her race for re-election 
 Rep. Lauren Boebert, R-Colo., a conservative firebrand who was caught up in several headline-grabbing controversies during her six years in Congress, has been defeated by Democratic challenger Eileen Laubacher, NBC News projects.
 Laubacher is a retired Navy rear admiral and Afghanistan war veteran who served on the National Security Council in the Biden administration.
 Rep. Lauren Boebert.   Bill Clark / CQ-Roll Call via Getty 
 Read the full story here. 
 2h ago / 3:00 PM EST Supreme Court to rule on Trump’s asylum ban 
 Taking up another key aspect of President Donald Trump’s hard-line immigration agenda, the Supreme Court on Friday agreed to decide whether the administration has the authority to ban asylum claims at the southern border.
 Although a federal judge ruled that the policy Trump enacted on the first day of his second term was unlawful, it has remained in effect while litigation continues.
 Read the full story here. 
 3h ago / 2:37 PM EST Alito says Supreme Court is caught between the president and a Congress that can ‘turn off the lights’ 
 Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito expressed concern about Congress’ potential use of the power of the purse against the high court in remarks at an event in Washington, D.C., Thursday night. 
 Speaking with conservative author Mollie Hemingway at a black-tie dinner for the annual Federalist Society’s National Lawyers Convention, Alito said the judiciary is the “least dangerous” branch of the government, and is “vulnerable to the executive and to Congress because they are more powerful.”
 Read the full story here. 
 3h ago / 1:43 PM EST Feds add D.C. terrorism charge for White House Correspondents’ Dinner gunman 
 A federal grand jury has added an attempted terrorism charge to the case of Cole Tomas Allen, the man arrested at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner Association dinner in April.
 Allen now faces a total of five counts, including a top charge of attempting to assassinate the president of the United States. If convicted, federal prosecutors could potentially seek a federal terrorism sentencing enhancement. Allen previously pleaded not guilty in connection with the April 25 incident. He has not pleaded in the new charge.
 Read the full story here. 
 4h ago / 12:59 PM EST Sen. Chris Van Hollen advocates 'shaking things up' in government after launching bid for majority leader 
 After announcing his bid to run for Senate majority leader last night, Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., said he favored "shaking things up" in the federal government in the wake of last week's midterm elections. 
 "It wasn’t a vote against government. It was a vote for a better government," Van Hollen said of Democrats' large election gains in remarks at Democrats' "What's Next" conference in Denver. 
 "We should not be preserving our institutions if they are not delivering for the American people, and we should be making delivering for the American people the single mission of our government, even when that means shaking things up. And that is why I’m running for the majority leader in the United States Senate," he said, drawing rousing applause from the audience. 
 Sen. Chris Van Hollen in Denver today.   Chet Strange / Bloomberg via Getty 
 Show more "What if we went toe-to-toe with the president to take on the fights that are too important to lose? Not just using the tools in our power, but by making the case to the American people to end the war, to protect health care, to stop our neighbors from being sent to foreign gulags, to defend our Constitution," he continued. "What if we took the incredible energy we saw around the country last week and made that the north star for the United States Senate?"
 Van Hollen is challenging Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., to lead the Democrats next year. Caucus members will hold a vote behind closed doors in December to choose their leadership for the next Congress. It requires a simple majority of the caucus.
 4h ago / 12:46 PM EST Jeffries ticks off House Democrats' priorities in the new Congress 
 During the interview at the What's Next conference, Jeffries outlined some of his party's priorities when it retakes the House majority early next year. He said some of them include:
 Reversing damage done to health care and Obamacare
 Ending Citizens United
 Banning members of Congress from trading stock
 Codifying abortion rights
 Banning mid-cycle redistricting and gerrymandering
 Investigating the Nvidia scandal 
 Jeffries in Denver today.   Chet Strange / Bloomberg via Getty Images 
 5h ago / 12:27 PM EST Hakeem Jeffries faces protesters at Democrats' What's Next conference 
 Protesters interrupt Rep. Jeffries at Democrats' 'What's Next' conference 01:51 
 Protesters inside the room at Democrats' "What's Next' conference in Denver screamed at House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., in protest today as he participated in an interview on stage about the party's agenda.
 First, a protester yelled that she was "scared for her future" and yelled, "When is it time for a Green New Deal? When is it time for Medicare for All?" Several protesters seemed to join in. 
 Other attendees chanted Jeffries' name. He's expected to be elected the first Black speaker of the House in the new year, with Democrats taking the majority. 
 Jeffries continued speaking amid the shouts from the audience. Another protester also yelled, "You are a f------ liar!'" The person appeared to be shouting about impeachment. 
 Demonstrators interrupt Rep. Hakeem Jeffries today in Denver.   Chet Strange / Bloomberg via Getty 
 5h ago / 12:01 PM EST Trump says that if the 'Iran crazies' are still in power after he leaves office, it would be a 'defeat' 
 Trump said in an interview with conservative radio host Hewitt yesterday that if the “Iran crazies” are still in power after he leaves office, that would be a “defeat” for him. 
 Hewitt brought up how Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Attorney General Todd Blanche have had to move to military bases and asked what would happen to Iranians if they killed a senior U.S. official. 
 “They will not exist very long … any longer,” Trump said. 
 5h ago / 11:45 AM EST 'F- the Iranian leadership': Bessent addresses move to military base after threats from Iran 
 Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had choice words for Iran today in response to him moving to a military base in light of threats from the adversary. 
 "You know what I got to say, Joe, is F- the Iranian leadership," Bessent said in an interview on CNBC with Joe Kernen and Rebecca Quick.
 "I’m not going to be cowered that they have initiated death threats against me," he continued. "The other members of the Cabinet were not going to be cowered, and it means what we are doing with Operation Economic Outcast is working."
 Show more Bessent said that he followed U.S. Secret Service instructions and moved from his home to a military base, adding that "one of the reasons I’ve had to move is because the Wall Street Journal printed a photo of my house the day I bought it." 
 "The editor, we pleaded with her not to print the location of my house, but she did anyway," Bessent told CNBC. "Highly irresponsible and dangerous, and things like that have to stop too."
 7h ago / 9:40 AM EST Trump says he wants to ‘get Cuba done’ when asked about use of military force 
 President Donald Trump signaled in a new interview that he could take military action against Cuba before he leaves office to topple the island’s communist regime.
 “I want to get Cuba done before I leave you,” Trump told conservative radio host Hugh Hewitt on Thursday when asked if he would order the use of military force against Cuba to free the nation.
 Read the full story here. 
 8h ago / 9:22 AM EST Iran-linked plots come into focus as U.S. pulls jets from British bases 
 Since World War II , the rolling green hills of Britain’s countryside have been home to American air bases — hosting the fighter planes that have projected Washington’s power from Kosovo to Iraq.
 The American military presence is rarely remarked on and often unnoticed by their British neighbors, but a flurry of incidents this week has brought this relationship into sharp focus.
 Read the full story here. 
 8h ago / 8:42 AM EST Democrats can’t wait until after Trump to produce results, James Talarico says 
 Texas Sen.-elect James Talarico told a gathering of Democrats yesterday that voters are expecting them to immediately deliver, and that means making Trump’s last two years in office the “most productive of any presidency in American history.”
 Talarico, who just made history by becoming the first Democrat elected senator in Texas since 1988, urged his party to put aside vitriol and distractions and immediately provide economic relief to Americans. Democrats won both chambers of Congress, but Trump will remain in the White House — and wield the veto pen — until 2029.
 James Talarico in Denver yesterday.   Chet Strange / Bloomberg via Getty 
 Read the full story here. 
 9h ago / 7:58 AM EST GOP chairs tell Jensen Huang, Nvidia they must commit to closed-door testimony by today 
 The GOP chairs of the House Select Committee on China, Foreign Affairs Committee and Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence sent Jensen Huang and a lawyer for Nvidia letters yesterday demanding they agree by this evening to give closed-door testimony. 
 Reps. John Moolenaar of Michigan, Brian Mast of Florida and Rick Crawford of Arkansas asked Huang, who resigned as CEO of Nvidia yesterday over reports that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese agent, and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter to appear before Congress in early December. 
 “As reports continue to come to light regarding Jensen Huang, NVIDIA, and MegaSpeed, there are clear national security concerns that need to be addressed immediately,” Mast, Moolenaar and Crawford wrote. “We need to know the full extent to which our national security has been put at risk.’ 
 They added: “This situation is a prime example of why Congress must immediately pass the AI OVERWATCH Act, Chip Security Act, MATCH Act, and Remote Access Security Act in the NDAA.”
 Show more Mast also asked Jeff Kessler, undersecretary for industry and security at the Commerce Department, to appear before the Foreign Affairs Committee.
 Mast told NBC News yesterday that Huang agreed to brief lawmakers, though the date and venue were still being negotiated. The letter to Huang asked that he appear before the committee Dec. 1 for a “closed-door, transcribed interview,” adding that a subpoena would be issued if Huang did not confirm the interview by this evening.
 Similar letters were sent to Teter and Kessler, who were asked to appear Dec. 2 and Dec. 3, respectively. Teter was also warned that a subpoena would be sent if he does not confirm the interview by this evening. 
 10h ago / 7:38 AM EST Democrat Cindy Holscher defeats Republican Ty Masterson in Kansas governor’s race 
 Democratic state Sen. Cindy Holscher has narrowly won Kansas’ race for governor , NBC News projected yesterday, extending the party’s hold on the office in the red state.
 Holscher defeated Republican state Senate President Ty Masterson, who was backed by Trump , to succeed two-term Democratic Gov. Laura Kelly.
 Kansas gubernatorial candidate Cindy Holscher.   Evert Nelson / The Capital-Journal / USA Today via Imagn 
 While Trump carried Kansas — a state where registered Republicans outnumber registered Democrats nearly 2 to 1 — by double digits in the latest three presidential elections, polling had shown a close race down the stretch due mostly to voter frustrations with Trump and his handling of the economy. Democrats also benefited from increased attention on the traditionally conservative state as its Senate race tightened.
 Holscher’s victory came despite a nearly 3-to-1 Republican ad spending advantage in the general election, according to ad-tracking firm AdImpact.
 Read the full story here. 
 10h ago / 7:38 AM EST Howard Lutnick agrees to testify as bipartisan pressure grows over Nvidia scandal 
 Facing bipartisan pressure, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick agreed tonight to testify before Congress over national security concerns regarding the expanding Nvidia scandal.
 The announcement comes after Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., chair of the Senate Banking Committee, sent letters today to Lutnick and Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s CEO earlier in the day after reports that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
 “Secretary Lutnick has proactively agreed to appear voluntarily before the Banking Committee to address their questions,” Kristen Eichamer, a spokesperson for Lutnick, told NBC News.
 Read the full story here. 
 10h ago / 7:38 AM EST Sen. Chris Van Hollen says he will challenge Sen. Chuck Schumer for majority leader 
 Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., announced last night he will run for Senate majority leader, becoming the first to challenge Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., for the position.
 “In this election, the American people called for change. They called for a change from Donald Trump’s disastrous policies — but even bigger than that, a change from the status quo that isn’t working for working people,” Van Hollen said in a statement.
 Van Hollen’s move follows attempts by grassroots progressives — and some newly elected Democratic senators — to draft him for the position as some seek an alternative to Schumer.
 “It’s now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership. This is not about any one person — it’s about answering the call of the American people. That is why I’m running for Senate Majority Leader,” he added.
 Read the full story here. 
 10h ago / 7:38 AM EST Potential 2028 Democratic contenders discuss what's next for the party at Colorado conference 
 Democrats are holding their second day of a conference in Denver to talk about the midterms and what comes next as the party looks to take control of Congress. 
 Several potential 2028 contenders will speak today at the “What’s Next” conference, hosted by the group Majority Democrats, including Sens. Chris Van Hollen, Raphael Warnock, Ruben Gallego and Cory Booker, former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg and Rep. Ro Khanna.
